prompt:
Find what the Debian project officially states about the support period of a stable release, including LTS. Cite the Debian page and quote the relevant statement.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The Debian project officially states that the support life cycle for a stable release encompasses a total of five years. This period is divided into three years of full security support provided by the Debian Security Team, followed by two years of Long Term Support (LTS) managed by the Debian LTS team.

SOURCE: https://www.debian.org/releases/ | QUOTE: "The Debian release life cycle encompasses five years: the first three years of full support followed by two years of Long Term Support (LTS)." | CLAIM: The official support period for a Debian stable release is five years, consisting of three years of full support and two years of LTS.

SOURCE: https://wiki.debian.org/DebianReleases | QUOTE: "has (from release to the end of security updates) a total lifetime of 5 years (the first three years of full support followed by two years of Long Term Support (LTS))." | CLAIM: The total lifetime of a stable release, from initial release to the end of security updates, is five years.

SOURCE: https://www.debian.org/releases/stable/ | QUOTE: "The Debian 13 life cycle encompasses five years: the initial three years of full Debian support, until August 9th, 2028, and two years of Long Term Support (LTS), until June 30th, 2030." | CLAIM: An example of this policy is Debian 13, which receives full support for three years and LTS for the subsequent two years, ending in 2030.
